He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]]. Newell was a consensus [[five-star recruit]] in the class of 2024, earning the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup#Awards|2023 FIBA Under-19 World Cup Defensive MVP]]. ==Early life and high school career== Newell was born in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]], and grew up in [[Athens, Georgia]] before his family moved to [[Destin, Florida]] when he was ten years old.{{cite web|url=https://uga.rivals.com/news/five-star-asa-newell-s-life-and-career-come-full-circle-in-athens|title=Five-star Asa Newell's life and career comes full circle in Athens|first=Anthony|last=Dasher|website=[[Rivals.com]]|access-date=November 13, 2023}}{{Cite web |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Georgia, White land five-star forward Newell |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/38743692/georgia-mike-white-land-5-star-forward-asa-newell |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He initially attended [[Choctawhatchee High School]] in [[Fort Walton Beach, Florida]]. Newell averaged 14.7 points and 8.7 rebounds per game and was named the area Player of the Year by the ''[[Northwest Florida Daily News]]'' as a sophomore.{{cite web|url=https://www.nwfdailynews.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/07/30/daily-news-basketball-all-area-newell-sanders-jeadline-poy-coy-honorsdaily-news-basketball-all-area/10102095002/|title=Daily News Boys Basketball All-Area: Newell, Sanders headline POY/COY honors|work=[[Northwest Florida Daily News]]|date=July 30, 2022|access-date=November 13, 2023}} Newell transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]] prior to the start of his junior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.onlineathens.com/story/sports/college/bulldogs-extra/2023/11/09/asa-newell-georgia-basketball-college-basketball-recruiting-sec-basketball/71515275007/|title=Here's what Mike White |website=Online Athens |language=en-US}} He averaged 15.4 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.0 block in 29.0 minutes per game. Newell was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team. Following the season, he declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Georgia star freshman Asa Newell to enter 2025 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44601555/georgia-star-freshman-asa-newell-enter-2025-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=December 17, 2025 |date=April 9, 2025}} ==Professional career== On June 25, 2025, Newell was selected with the 23rd pick by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]], but was subsequently traded along with a future unprotected first-round pick to his hometown team, the [[Atlanta Hawks]], in exchange for the draft rights of his former high school teammate [[Derik Queen]].{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2025 |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire the Draft Rights of Asa Newell, the No. 23 Pick in the 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-the-draft-rights-of-asa-newell-the-no-23-pick-in-the-2025-nba-draft |access-date=July 18, 2025 |website=NBA.com}} ==National team career== Newell played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States under-17 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/basketball/asa-newell-announces-top-4-indiana-georgia-texas-gonzaga-alabama-2024-5-star-top-10-prospect-montverde-basketball-recruiting|title=Asa Newell Announces Top 4, Indiana Not Included|first=Daniel|last=Olinger|website=[[SI.com]]|date=September 20, 2023|access-date=November 14, 2023}} Newell was also named to the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-19 basketball team]] to play in the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/recruiting/gonzaga-schedules-visit-with-five-star-forward-asa-newell|title=Asa Newell visiting Gonzaga;
